question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $f$ as the composite function

$$
f={6}^{u},\,u=-3{x}^{2}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}u}={6}^{u}\ln(6),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-6x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={6}^{u}\ln(6)\cdot (-6x) \\ & =(-6x)\cdot {6}^{u}\ln(6) \\ & =-6x\cdot {6}^{-3{x}^{2}}\ln(6).\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=3\cdot {4}^{u},\,u={x}^{2}-1.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=3\cdot {4}^{u}\ln4,\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =3\cdot {4}^{u}\ln4\cdot 2x \\  & =6x\cdot {4}^{{x}^{2}-1}\ln4.\end{aligned}
$$
